text:
maya_support: high-severity support escalation — multiple customers in us-west-2 reporting sharp p95/p99 regressions since 11:58 UTC. p95 ~120ms -> ~520ms, p99 >1.2s. Customer traces show repeated SYN retransmits to our inference-proxy edge. escalating to eng-sre + netops.

deploy-bot: ALERT: infra.api.inference-proxy.us-west-2 p95=540ms p99=1.25s (11:58 UTC) — paging eng-sre.

ana_sre: typo: tagging ana_sre: I'm looking. Edge logs show bursts of SYN retransmits and retransmit RTOs from our anycast POP -> aws egress IPs. Requesting traceroute + tcpdump from affected host.

maya_support: attaching quick captures from customer and our edge (scrubbed IPs):

Customer traceroute:
```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.example (52.12.34.56), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.8 ms  0.7 ms  0.7 ms
 2  198.51.100.5  12.2 ms  12.3 ms  12.1 ms
 3  34.201.12.8  30.5 ms  30.6 ms  30.7 ms
 4  52.12.34.56  120.9 ms  121.1 ms  121.0 ms
```

Edge tcpdump snippet (edge IP 34.201.12.8 -> 52.12.34.56):
```
12:00:01.123456 IP 34.201.12.8.54012 > 52.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
12:00:01.624789 IP 34.201.12.8.54012 > 52.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmission)
12:00:02.125901 IP 34.201.12.8.54012 > 52.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmission)
12:00:02.425000 IP 52.12.34.56.443 > 34.201.12.8.54012: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, length 0
```

joe_netops: I'm seeing correlated BGP withdraws from peer 198.51.100.5 around 11:59 that cause path flip to a higher-latency egress. There's also evidence of SYN drops on the egress blade (hardware counters) coincident with an ACL change pushed at 11:55 by the colo provider. Could be a mis-ordered ACL that rate-limits new TCP handshakes.

liam_plat: proposed mitigations:
- Short-term: pin affected customer traffic to the alternative egress path (route-policy prefer-local) to avoid peer 198.51.100.5.
- Reduce connection churn: temporarily lower default inference client keepalive/batch size for affected token group.
- Enable SYN health probe: detect repeated SYN-RTOs and failover automatically.

ana_sre: applied route-policy avoid-peer-198.51.100.5 at 12:05 UTC for the affected POP. Also decreased routing preference to favor same-AZ egress for api tokens that hit the busy pod.

joe_netops: confirmed we contacted colo and they reverted the ACL change at 12:07 UTC. Hardware SYN drop counters dropping to normal by 12:08.

karen_csm: updating customers: told them we pinned routes temporarily and are monitoring. they reported improved latency within minutes.

maya_support: customer confirmation: after mitigation their p95 is ~140ms and p99 ~220ms. asking eng-sre to monitor 30m and prepare postmortem with timeline.

deploy-bot: RESOLVED: infra.api.inference-proxy.us-west-2 p95 <200ms (12:14 UTC).

ana_sre: preliminary root cause: transient ACL change on colo peer 198.51.100.5 that caused packet drops of initial SYNs, triggering retransmits and route flaps to higher-latency peers. Action items:
- Netops: ensure colo ACL deploy checklist and automated egress health check (assigned joe_netops).
- Platform: implement SYN failure detector and automated routing fallback (assigned liam_plat).
- Support: notify affected customers and include timeline (assigned maya_support/karen_csm).

maya_support: thanks all — will open an incident/PM for the postmortem and follow up with customer-facing note. :thumbsup:
summary: Support escal for p95/p99 spikes in us-west-2 due to SYN retransmits caused by colo ACL change; temporary route pin and ACL revert mitigated impact.
